Autonomous Grimoire.text:
{{Spell InfoBox|image=Autonomous_Grimoire.png|type=Spell Summon|rarity=Rare|mana_cost1=40|mana_cost2=50|mana_cost3=60|hp1=40|hp2=65|hp3=100|summon_limit1=3|summon_limit2=3|summon_limit3=3|misc_a_1=Records and uses the first shooting spell on the right|misc_b_1=Grimoire grants a MP Regen speed equivalent to 50% of the summoning wand|misc_a_2=Records and uses the first shooting spell on the right|misc_b_2=Grimoire grants a MP Regen speed equivalent to 75% of the summoning wand|misc_a_3=Records and uses the first shooting spell on the right|misc_b_3=Grimoire grants a MP Regen speed equivalent to 110% of the summoning wand}}The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Rarity|Rare]] [[Spells|Spell]] of [[Spell Types|Type]]: Spell Summon. When the default spell is cast, it summons a floating book that casts the spell in the wand to the right.

The Grimoire can cast either projectile spells or summon creatures.

* If it is used to cast projectile spells, the Grimoire will automatically shoot at the nearest enemy in range.
* If it is used to cast summons, it will begin summoning creatures. If the Grimoire dies, all summons it controlled die as well. If a Grimoire summons after reaching the summoning limit, one of the existing summons will be killed and a new one is spawned near the player. This may be useful with some builds but generally hurts DPS because the summon already in combat disappears and the newly created summon has to move into place to begin combat with enemies. This can be prevented by enabling a setting in Settings > Gameplay > Summon Limit > On. With this setting on, the Grimoire will summon until the limit is hit and then stop, only summoning a new creature if an existing creature dies.

Grimoires can also summon more Grimoires, for example you could have Grimoire > Grimoire > [[Pop]] which would summon 3 parent Grimoires which would each have 3 child Grimoires which would each have 5 Pops for a total of 45 Pops. Granted, it takes a while for all of the child Grimoires and Pops to be summoned and that also assumes that none of them die in combat.

'''Description:''' Some mages enjoy using magic to make books turn pages automatically, but obviously these books possess more powerful abilities.
[[Category:Spell]]
[[Category:Spell Type: Spell Summon]]
[[Category:Rarity: Rare]]

Chests.text:
[[File:Chest Behind Spike Wall.png|thumb|A chest that can only be reached by flying or trickery]]
Lost Chests are scattered around the world outside the camp. Often simply in plain sight, but other times hidden behind walls or over spike pits. They can also appear in Side Rooms, such as the Cursed Chest Room. Chests come in a variety of forms, and most require some sort of sacrifice to unlock.

== Chest Types ==

=== Cursed Chests ===
Require the hero to accept [[Curses]] in order to open the chest. The hero can usually tell which curse they will have to accept before they open it, though some Curses and effects can render them unreadable.  Cursed Chests often appear in [[Side Room|Side Rooms]], where many can appear at once.

=== Locked Chests ===
The most common type; locked chests require a key to open, and are usually in plain sight.[[File:Capture.png|thumb|An unlocked chest hidden between two rows of trees (one of which was destroyed).]]

=== Spike Chests ===
Spike Chests are another common type of chest, and require a sacrifice of health (10 hp) to open. They can kill the player.

=== Unlocked Chests ===
A rare type that, when it appears, is almost always hidden.

Area Boost.text:
{{Spell InfoBox|image=Area_Boost.png|type=Spell Passive|rarity=Rare|misc_a_1=Copies Level 1|misc_a_2=Copies Level 2|misc_a_3=Copies Level 3}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Rarity|Rare]] [[Spells|Spell]] of [[Spell Types|Type]]: Spell Passive. It effectively is a rather advanced variant of the [[Mimicry Cube]].

{{PAGENAME}} takes up 4 slots to equip into a wand, then the first spell that is placed to the right of it will be duplicated into every other wand you are holding, in the leftmost position, including the "host" wand using {{PAGENAME}}. This will not consume a slot in those wands, the effect is created in a new, free, locked slot; correspondingly, copying a spell that needs something else to the left of it to work such as [[Echo]] or [[Duet]] is not recommended, unless you use {{PAGENAME}} twice to load a triggering spell and then one of those two.

* Note, the copied spell is put to the left of any already existing locked slots on a wand, such as the Soul Set's natural [[Wand Spirit|Wand Spirits]].
* If {{PAGENAME}} is fit twice into two separate wands, the copied spell in the higher slot will go first (i.e. a copied spell set in wand 2 will take effect first before a copied spell in wand 3)

Like with [[Mimicry Cube]], the level of {{PAGENAME}} determines up to what level of the copied spell it will duplicate, and a high level {{PAGENAME}} cannot create a higher level copy of a low level spell.

'''SPECIAL INTERACTIONS'''
* [[Magic Vine]]: Is never considered to have the stacking effect from empty slots to the right of it, so will always be one single iteration of the buff.
* Multi-slot spells like [[Arcane Barrier]] or [[Core of Flame]]: Do not take up their extra slots, they only show 1 single slot at the beginning of the wand but the effects are still at full strength.
* [[Capacity Expansion Stone]]: Extra slots are still added to the far right end of the wands as normal.
[[Category:Spell]]
[[Category:Spell Type: Spell Passive]]
[[Category:Rarity: Rare]]

{{Spell InfoBox|image=Mana_Absorption.png|desc=Legendary mana-absorbing spell|type=Spell Projectiles|rarity=Epic|mana_cost1=8|dmg1=24|cd1=-0.2s|crit_rate1=40%|misc_a_1=Restores the mana spent for the casting wand when hitting an enemy for the first time|misc_b_1=Unable to craft}}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an [[Rarity|Epic]] [[Spells|Spell]] of [[Spell Types|Type]]: Spell Projectiles. While this spell doesn't do much damage or change with upgrades, it can provide a steady flow of mana to the wand casting it.

'''Description:''' Returns mana to you after completing its mission gratefully, but if you can cast it with less MP, what a deal

'''How to get free mana:''' Mana Absorption is not only useful for shooting itself for free; it can also be used to generate more mana than you spend, allowing you to sustain larger mana costs from other spells. The way the spell typically works is by dividing the mana returned among the amount of projectiles released. This means you can't simply put [[Split]] or [[Multi-Shot]] before it to gain free mana. Instead, you should increase the number of spells that will release Mana Absorption, or use spells that will release multiple Mana Absorptions themselves.

Here are some builds that will generate free mana:

* [[Arcane Nova]] + Mana Absorption 
* [[Multi-Shot]] + any projectile spell + any [[Trigger spells|Trigger spell]] + Mana Absorption
* [[Multi-Shot]] + [[Split]] + Mana Absorption 
* Any projectile spell + [[Dazzling Fireworks]] + Mana Absorption

Duet.text:
{{Spell InfoBox|image=Duet.png|type=Spell Boost|rarity=Normal|misc_a_1=Casts the spell on the right at the completion of the spell on the left|misc_b_1=The spell on the right inherits 30% of the damage from the spell on the left|misc_a_2=Casts the spell on the right at the completion of the spell on the left|misc_b_2=The spell on the right inherits 60% of the damage from the spell on the left|misc_a_3=Casts the spell on the right at the completion of the spell on the left|misc_b_3=The spell on the right inherits 120% of the damage from the spell on the left}}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Rarity|Normal]] [[Spells|Spell]] of [[Spell Types|Type]]: Spell Boost. The right spell becomes more powerful based on the damage of the left spell.

Even though the spell description does not mention it, the damage bonus from Duet applies to all spells inside the payload of duet, except those separated by another [[Trigger spells|Trigger spell.]] 

Example 1:

Wand with simultaneous casting 1

[[Meteor]] + [[Duet]] + [[Volley]] + [[Magic Bullet]] + [[Laser]]

The duet damage bonus will apply to both the magic bullet and the laser. 

Example 2:

Wand with simultaneous casting 2

[[Meteor]] + [[Duet]] + [[Magic Bullet]] + [[Dazzling Fireworks]] + [[Laser]] + [[Butterfly]] + [[Rainbow]]

The duet damage bonus is applied to the magic bullet and rainbow but not to laser and butterfly, because those are inside of [[Trigger spells|trigger spell]] payload.

'''DPS spells and Duet''': When applying the duet damage to spells that do damage over time (those that have "DPS" in brackets) the Duet damage bonus is added to the overall damage per second. This means you will be hitting the enemy for dps divided by the [[Tick rate]] of the spell for each tick. 

Exception to this rule is [[Skull of the Cthulhu]] which gains x1.75 Duet damage on all its ticks.

Lightning dash does damage multiple times but does not have a DPS tag, so it benefits normally from the duet damage boost.

Damage Calculation.text:
This page is work in progress, info may be incomplete

'''Damage formula'''

Here is how damage is calculated in Magicraft:

((('''Spell base damage'''  + '''Base damage increase''') × '''Spell damage multiplier''' + '''Mirrored damage''') 

   × '''Final damage multiplier''' 

   × '''Conditional final damage''' 

   + '''Bubble growth damage''') 

       × '''Crit multiplier''' × '''Enemy damage taken de-buff'''

'''Base damage:''' Damage a spell does when hitting an enemy when unmodified.

'''Base damage increase:''' Base damage increase from things like [[Enchanting Coin]] from coins, [[Fierce Dragon Breath]] over time, [[Supernova]] from charging, and [[Blast Surge]] only if spell has a radius, [[Dimension Walker]] off of current mana.

'''Spell damage multiplier:''' Changed by [[Relics]] (additive), [[Curses]] (additive), spells like [[DMG Enhanced]] (additive), [[Overload]] (additive), [[Wands|Energizer wand]] (additive) when criteria is met, [[Reflection]] (multiplicative) and [[Energy Saving Mode]] (multiplicative). Total curse + relics damage can be seen on the character screen in the pause menu.

'''Mirrored damage:''' That's the damage that [[Duet]] gives to the payload. Most spells marked with (DPS) in the tool tip will divide the Mirrored damage over their [[Tick rate|Ticks]] of damage, except for [[Skull of the Cthulhu]] for some reason it gets x1.75 Duet damage for all ticks.

'''Final damage:''' Multiplier affected by [[Capacity Expansion Stone]] (multiplicative), [[Wands|Wand]] stat of final damage (multiplicative), [[Thunderstorm]] when meeting condition of hitting a single enemy (multiplicative). 

'''Conditional final damage multiplier:''' Affected by [[Shining Star Arrow]] with crit condition met and [[Skull of the Cthulhu]] scaling from max MP. Formula for [[Skull of the Cthulhu]] damage multiplier from mp is: 1 + Max mp × 0.001/0.002 (for skull+/skull++ respectively). Why separate it from Final damage? Because, unlike Final Damage, the Conditional final damage multiplier will be applied when calculating the damage a spell will supply to spells after [[Duet]]. [[Skull of the Cthulhu]] mp to damage multiplier also gets recalculated when [[Fusion Summon|Fusion Summoning]] with more skulls. 

'''Bubble growth damage:''' [[Condensed Water Bubble]] is a weird spell in that it's damage gain from lifetime is not affected by multiplicative damage modifications. The formula for Bubble growth damage is: Lifetime in seconds x 0.2/0.25/0.35 depending on bubble level x 100/170/290 base damage x Spell damage multiplier without the [[Energy Saving Mode]].

'''Crit multiplier:''' Applied if the roll for a crit succeeds, the multiplier is x2 by default is able to upgraded with [[Relics|Blade of Fury]].

'''Enemy damage taken de-buff:''' De-buff applied by [[Magic Bullet]] making enemies take x1.5/x2 damage when hitting them with bullet+ and bullet++ respectively.


'''About how duet takes damage from the spell on the left'''

Resulting mirrored damage that a spell will provide when using [[Duet]] is calculated as followed: 

((('''Spell base damage'''  + '''Base damage increase''') × '''Spell damage multiplier''') + '''Mirrored damage''' + '''Bubble growth damage''') × '''Conditional final damage multiplier''' × 0.3/0.6/1.2 (depending on [[Duet]] level)

Note: In duet calculation spell base damage for most dps spells is its total damage over a second (the number on the tool-tip), except [[Skull of the Cthulhu]] for which it takes its one tick of damage number.

Note: Magicraft rounds a lot, after like every single math operation... that means that the order of the multipliers (and potentially even the order of the separate sources of multipliers)  being applied matters. <sub>I am not figuring it out, good luck.😁</sub>

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Rarity|Normal]] [[Spells|Spell]] of [[Spell Types|Type]]: Spell Boost. It drops spells from the sky and causes damage in an area where they hit the ground.

== Interactions ==

* [[Black Hole]]: Creates a large explosion area on the location of impact.
* [[Evil Slayer Sword]]: Drops the sword in a large area, with a minor offset impact location closer to the caster, based on the cursor location. [[Precise Shot]] reduces this scatter effect, but does not eliminate it.
* [[Dimension Walker]]: Lands on the caster, repeating the impact to the right of the initial impact point, repeating until the spell runs out.

Magic Vine.text:
{{Spell InfoBox|image=Magic_Vine.png|type=Spell Passive|rarity=Rare|misc_a_1=MP Regen of the wand +20%|misc_a_2=MP Regen of the wand +35%|misc_a_3=MP Regen of the wand +TBD|misc_b_1=Max MP of the wand +10%|misc_b_2=Max MP of the wand +20%|misc_b_3=Max MP of the wand +TBD}}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Rarity|Rare]] [[Spells|Spell]] of [[Spell Types|Type]]: Spell Passive. When placed in a wand, it increases the wand's mana regen and mana capacity, with a stacking effect depending on how many wand slots to the right of it are empty.

* The benefit stacks additively for each empty wand slot to the right of {{PAGENAME}}, so 2 empty slots would double it, 3 empty slots would triple it, etc...the slot that {{PAGENAME}} itself is in also counts as one iteration.
* The slots to the right of {{PAGENAME}} are not locked; other spells can be placed in them as normal.
* The benefit effect will not pass over an equipped spell to fill other empty slots to the right of it; it will only work in the first unbroken chain of empty slots immediately to the right of {{PAGENAME}}.

Relics.text:
'Relics' are items gained from [[Relic Rooms]] (and random chest drops) that grant you special powers. Relics are the opposite of [[Curses]], though some can still have negative effects. Like [[Spells]], Relics are lost on [[Death]]. However, unlike [[Spells]], Relics are entirely passive & cannot be dropped or removed. Relics can, however, be upgraded or re-rolled by [[Potions]] or other Relics.

If you defeat the boss of a level without taking any HP damage (you can still lose shields), the game will open another room before proceeding with Crimsom Relics. You will have the chance to get 3 special Epic Relics, each one at the cost of decreasing your maximum HP by an amount .

While playing on Nightmare 2, there is a 1% chance for a relic to be Epic. On Nightmare 3, this chance is 1.6%.

Shadow Serpent + Track.text:
== How does this build work ==
Spawn as many [[Ghost Snake|Ghost Snakes]] as you can and have as high damage as possible. Use [https://magicraft.fandom.com/wiki/Tracking Tracking] and [[spells]] like [[Orbit]] or [[Accelerator]] to increase the speed and duration of the Snakes.

== How to get this build fast ==

=== Method 1 ===

# Choose the Original Class and try to get Tracking in a shop or any other rare spell
# Go into a forge and combine your [[Magic Bullet|Magic Bullets]]
# Roll the Magic Bullet+ to a Ghost Snake+
# Roll, if you don't already have it, your rare spell to Tracking

=== Method 2 (only works with Tier 2 Dash Class) ===

# Try to get any common spell
# Go into a forge and roll it to Ghost Snake
# Replace the [[Lightning Dash]] with Ghost Snake

Potions.text:
0Potions are one-time consumables that occupy slots at the bottom right of the screen. At start of game, you only have one potion slot - but this can be upgraded using [[Blood Of The Old Gods]]. Potions have various magical effects; some of which only last a few seconds, while others may affect a whole run. For example: by removing [[Curses]], boosting stats, unlocking all doors, multiplying keys, granting shields, and even summoning [[Chests]]. Like [[Relics]] and [[Spells]], all potions effects expire on [[Death]] and all unused potions are lost.

== Finding Potions ==
Potions are available from as drops from enemies, chests, and bosses. They can also be bought from the [[Shop]], and the [[Potion Shop]].

Potion Shop.text: The [[Potions|Potion]] Shop is a [[Sideroom]] that appears next to the [[Shop]]. It is a special area that contains only random potions for sale.

Side Room.text:
Side Rooms are rarely-encountered areas that adjoin both normal and non-combat rooms. Siderooms in combat areas are usually locked and require a [[Key]], or other special circumstances. Some [[Relics]] & effects can guarantee certain Side Rooms.

==Combat Area Side Rooms==
These rooms are always locked or sealed in some way, and generally either require a key or a special event to open. Most 'Combat Area' Side Rooms are puzzles, assault courses, or otherwise challenges to the player. Combat Area Side Rooms are the most common form of Side Room you will encounter.  These include:

* Rooms full of [[Chests|Cursed Chests]].
* Spinning Fire Wheel Rooms
* Assault Courses
* Dark Room Assault Courses
* Puzzle Button Rooms
* Memory Sequence Rooms

== Shop & WitchWorks Side Rooms ==
Sometimes the [[Shop]] and [[WitchWorks]] contain various Side Rooms, which can appear on the left or right of the main area. These include:

* The [[Potion Shop]].
* The [[Rune Circle]].

== Boss Area Side Rooms ==
The rarest and most dangerous Side Rooms are the secret [[Blood Rooms]] that only adjoin certain (randomly chosen) Bosses. These can only be accessed by defeating the bosses without taking damage. At the current time, these are the only known [[Magicraft Wiki|Boss Monster]] side rooms.

Shining Star Arrow.text:
{{Spell InfoBox|image=Shining_Star_Arrow.png|type=Spell Projectiles|rarity=Normal|mana_cost1=27|mana_cost2=35|mana_cost3=46|dmg1=78|dmg2=148|dmg3=281|misc_a_1=Charged Casting|misc_b_1=Critical Rate increases by 25% per second during channeling|misc_c_1=When Critical rate exceeds 33%, final damage x150%|misc_a_2=Charged Casting|misc_b_2=Critical Rate increases by 25% per second during channeling|misc_c_2=When Critical rate exceeds 66%, final damage x170%|misc_a_3=Charged Casting|misc_b_3=Critical Rate increases by 25% per second during channeling|misc_c_3=When Critical rate exceeds 100%, final damage x200%}}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Rarity|Normal]] [[Spells|Spell]] of [[Spell Types|Type]]: Spell Projectiles. When the default spell is cast, it fires out a small projectile while knocking the player back slightly. This spell can be charged up for more damage by holding down the cast button. *The exceptions are:

**Unique Spells can only be obtained under special conditions:
***[[Enchanting Coin]] can be obtained by defeating the coin spider which spawns by destroying objects in Chapter 2. It is not guaranteed spawn every run.

* Without Nightmare Mode, the chance to get an epic spell in a Spell room without any Spell Focus upgrades from [[Lilian]] is 1%. With Spell Focus, each spell has a 0.66% chance to be Epic. '''Penetration'''

[[Penetration]] allows other spells to hit a target multiple times, but the spell needs to re-enter the enemy hit-box to be able to hit the same target again. [[Lightning Dash]] and [[Boomerang Blade]] are special in that they have penetration, but can also hit the same target multiple times without leaving their hit-box. However the tick-rate when doing so is relatively slow at only 3 hits per second. What you can do is exploit the "leave the hit-box to hit again" mechanic by either [[Track|Tracking]] the edge of the enemy hit-box or increasing their speed with [[Accelerator]] making them shake in and out of the enemy hit-boxes rapidly.

Upgrade Window.text:
[[File:Upgrade Window.png|thumb|The Upgrade Window in the Camp]]
[[File:Upgraded Upgrade Window.png|thumb|A partly upgraded upgrade window]]
While in the Hermit Camp, you can talk to the blue girl to access the upgrade window. This window allows you to pay [[Crystals]] from defeated enemies in order to upgrade your stats, as well as the 'prizes' of the various rooms you encounter during the game. To upgrade everything you need 48 [[Blood of the Old Gods]] and 3051 Crystals.

== Upgrade the Window ==
The {{PAGENAME}} can be expanded using Blood of the Old Gods to expose more available upgrades.

==No Upgrades==
Without any upgrades you get access to the following upgrades:
*Increase your Max Wand Slots by 1 per upgrade. The max is +3 and to upgrade it to the max you need 551 Crystals.
*Increase your Max Backpack Slots by 1 per upgrade. The max is +10 and to upgrade it to the max you need 195 Crystals.
*Increase your Initial Coins by 6 per upgrade. The max is +52 and to upgrade it to the max you need 370 Crystals.
*Increase your Starting [[Max HP]] by 5 per upgrade. The max is +50 and to upgrade it to the max you need 425 Crystals.

== First Upgrade ==
The first upgrade unlocks following upgrades:
*+33% increased Rarity Chance for Relics and Spells per upgrade. The max is x200% and to upgrade one of them to the max you need 95 Crystals.
*+3 extra [[Health]] gained from completing [[Health Room|Health Rooms]]. The max is +12 and to upgrade it to the max you need 199 Crystals.

== Second Upgrade ==
The second upgrade unlocks following upgrades:
*Increase your Max MP by 15 per upgrade. The max is +75 and to upgrade to the maximum you need 495 Crystals.
*Increase your MP regen rate by 1 per upgrade. The max is +5 and to upgrade to the max you need 495 Crystals.

Trigger spells.text:
Some spells in magicraft release other spells when a certain criteria is met. 

List of Trigger spells:

* [[Duet]]
* [[Fuse]]
* [[Echo]]
* [[Serial]]
* [[Dazzling Fireworks]]
* [[Twine]]
* [[Arcane Nova]]
* [[Autonomous Grimoire]]

'''Creating payload'''

When casting any of these spells they will take the simultaneous casting number you have and look to add that many spells to its "payload". The payload will then release when the condition of the spell is met. 

Things inside and outside of the payload will have separate effects of [[Multi-Shot]] and [[Duet]] damage bonus.

Template:Dialogue/doc.text:
{{t|Dialogue}} facilitates the writing of dialogue in a standard format. The template can handle most standard formats of writing dialogue, and can be indented, bulleted or numbered. '''This template ''cannot'' be subst:'d'''. This template uses the [[w:Help:Lua|Lua templating language]], and more information can be found [[w:c:dev:Global_Lua_Modules/Dialogue|on the Global Lua Module page]]. '''For a traditional wikitext version of this template, see [[w:c:templates:Template:Dialogue/wikitext|Dialogue on Templates Wiki]]'''. ==Syntax== This is how to write the template in [[w:Help:wikitext|wikitext]] onto your article: 
{{dialogue
|short=full
|short=full
|short=full
...
|Character|Speech
|Character|Speech
|Character|Speech
...
|cite = dialogue description
}}
These parameters are explained more fully below. ==Parameters== '''Named parameters specify name shortcuts. They are all optional.''' They are placed at the top of the template call, like this: 
{{dialogue
|short=full
|short=full
|short=full
...
Name shortcuts apply to your main dialogue text. If you use a shortcut specified here for a character name, then the full name will be replaced for it. Named parameters of the form "mood1", "mood2", "mood3", etc., up to "mood10", specify moods for the corresponding line number (e.g. "mood1" specifies line 1). They are placed in a line like this: 
...
|Character|Speech|mood1=angry
|Character|Speech|mood2=quiet
|Character|Speech|mood3=ecstatic
...
Positional parameters form the text of the dialogue (i.e. any line not containing an "=" will be construed as part of the dialogue. :;Parameter 1 ''(required)'' : Character name speaking :;Parameter 2 ''(optional)'' : Line to speak :;Parameter 3 ''(optional)'' : Next character :;Parameter 4 ''(optional)'' : Next line :;Parameter 5 ''(optional)'' : Next character :;Parameter 6 ''(optional)'' : Next line :;Parameter 7 ''(optional)'' : so on... Note: if any character is called "action" then that line will be construed as an action line. It still counts as a ''line'' nonetheless. To write a dialogue description/source, use cite = ==Examples== Here is an example of a full template usage: 
{{dialogue
|harry=Harry Enfield
|bryan=Bryan Adams

|harry|Hello!                |mood1=happy
|bryan|Oh hello there        |mood2=surprised
|harry|How are you?          |mood3=inquisitive
|bryan|Quite fine thank you. |mood4=reserved
|harry|Oh that's spiffing.   |mood5=spiffed
|bryan|It is, isn't it?!     |mood6=multo-spiffed
|harry|Quite so.             |mood7=bored
|bryan|Well, I'm off!        |mood8=joyous
|harry|Ta-ta!                |mood9=relieved
|bryan|Au revoir!            |mood10=sarcastic
}}
The above would generate: {{dialogue |harry=Harry Enfield |bryan=Bryan Adams |harry|Hello! |mood1=happy |bryan|Oh hello there |mood2=surprised |harry|How are you? |mood3=inquisitive |bryan|Quite fine thank you. |mood4=reserved |harry|Oh that's spiffing. |mood5=spiffed |bryan|It is, isn't it?! |mood6=multo-spiffed |harry|Quite so. |mood7=bored |bryan|Well, I'm off! |mood8=joyous |harry|Ta-ta! |mood9=relieved |bryan|Au revoir! |mood10=sarcastic }} The below code demonstrates examples of extended use: 
{{dialogue
|george=Georgie Boy
|rachel=Rachel

|action|Enter: George and Rachel
|george|Good morrow dearest Rachel!|mood2=happy
|action|Rachel turns to see him
|rachel|Oh, George, it's you!
|george|...
|rachel|Why won't you say anything?!|mood6=worried
|action|Enter: Guards
|Guards|We are announcing George's arrest!
|rachel|Oh my!|mood9=horrified
|action|George is dragged away.
}}
The above would generate: {{dialogue |george=Georgie Boy |rachel=Rachel |action|Enter: George and Rachel |george|Good morrow dearest Rachel!|mood2=happy |action|Rachel turns to see him |rachel|Oh, George, it's you! |george|... |rachel|Why won't you say anything?!|mood6=worried |action|Enter: Guards |Guards|We are announcing George's arrest! |rachel|Oh my!|mood9=horrified |action|George is dragged away. }} ===Notes=== You can number, bullet or indent your dialogue: 
:{{dialogue|Me|Hello|You|Howdido!}}
:{{dialogue|Me|Hello|You|Howdido!}} 
#{{dialogue|Me|Hello|You|Howdido!}}
#{{dialogue|Them|Good afternoon|Us|What a load of rubbish!}}
#{{dialogue|Me|Hello|You|Howdido!}} #{{dialogue|Them|Good afternoon|Us|What a load of rubbish!}} 
*{{dialogue
|angel=Fortitude
|angel|I am an angel!|Crowd|We don't believe you!}}
*{{dialogue
|angel=Fortitude
|angel|But I'm being quite serious!|Crowd|Too bad for you then!}}
*{{dialogue |angel=Fortitude |angel|I am an angel!|Crowd|We don't believe you!}} *{{dialogue |angel=Fortitude |angel|But I'm being quite serious!|Crowd|Too bad for you then!}} You will get the odd spacing error (e.g. "Speech") if you lay out your dialogue on multiple lines. [[Category:Quote templates]][[Category:Template documentation]]

Template:Clear/doc.text:
;Description This template allows you to clear the left side, right side, or both sides of the page. Clearing means that the content following the template will not be displayed until the existing content on the specified sides (for example, "hanging" or floating images or blocks) is displayed completely. This template is often used so that the text does not flow around unrelated images. The template adds the following code to the page:
(the value after clear depends on the parameters). This code affects elements with the CSS property float, including files floated to the side (for example, [[File:Image.png|right]]). ;Syntax * To clear both sides of the page, add the code {{t|Clear}}. * To clear only the left side of the page, add the code {{t|Clear|left}}. * To clear only the right side of the page, add the code {{t|Clear|right}}. You can also use {{t|-}} instead of {{t|Clear}} as a shorthand call for this template. __NOTOC__ ;Example 

=== Section 1 ===
[[File:Example.jpg|200px|right]]
Section 1 text.

=== Section 2 ===
Section 2 text.
{{Clear|right}}

=== Section 3 ===
Section 3 text.
This code produces the following result: ---- === Section 1 === [[File:Example.jpg|200px|right]] Section 1 text. === Section 2 === Section 2 text. {{Clear|right}} === Section 3 === Section 3 text. ---- As you can see above, the example image added in section 1 is displayed to the right and extends down through section 2, while the {{t|Clear}} template is called at the end of the second section, resulting in the example image not being next to section 3. Thus, one use of the {{t|Clear}} template is to control which elements are displayed next to which other elements. == See also == * [https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/clear CSS property clear on MDN] * [https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/float CSS property float on MDN] [[Category:General wiki templates]][[Category:Template documentation]]

Template:Cite web/doc.text:
__NOTOC__ This template is used to [[Wikipedia:WP:CITE|cite sources]] in Wikipedia. It is specifically for web sites which are not news sources. This template replaces deprecated [[Wikipedia:Template:Teb reference|template:web reference]]. It provides lower case parameters only. A general discussion of the use of templates for adding citation of open-source web content to Wikipedia articles is available at [[Wikipedia:Citation templates|citation templates]]. This page uses [[w:Wikia:Licensing|Creative Commons Licensed]] content from [[w:c:Wookieepedia:Template:Cite web|Wookieepedia]] == Usage == ;Common form for cases where little is known about authorship of the page (with current date) {{Cite web |url= |title= |accessdate={{CURRENTYEAR}}-{{CURRENTMONTH}}-{{CURRENTDAY2}} |format= |work= }} ;Using last, first (with current date) {{Cite web |url= |title= |accessdate={{CURRENTYEAR}}-{{CURRENTMONTH}}-{{CURRENTDAY2}} |last= |first= |authorlink= |coauthors= |date= |year= |month= |format= |work= |publisher= |pages= |language= |archiveurl= |archivedate= |quote= }} ;Using author (with current date) {{Cite web |url= |title= |accessdate={{CURRENTYEAR}}-{{CURRENTMONTH}}-{{CURRENTDAY2}} |author= |authorlink= |coauthors= |date= |year= |month= |format= |work= |publisher= |pages= |language= |archiveurl= |archivedate= |quote= }} ;Using non-linked retrieved date, last, first {{Cite web |url= |title= |accessmonthday= |accessyear= |last= |first= |authorlink= |coauthors= |date= |year= |month= |format= |work= |publisher= |pages= |language= |archiveurl= |archivedate= |quote= }} ;Using non-linked retrieved date, author {{Cite web |url= |title= |accessmonthday= |accessyear= |author= |authorlink= |coauthors= |date= |year= |month= |format= |work= |publisher= |pages= |language= |archiveurl= |archivedate= |quote= }} ;All parameters, horizontal format (delete the ones you don't need) {{Cite web |url= |title= |accessdate= |accessmonthday= |accessdaymonth = |accessyear= |author= |last= |first= |authorlink= |coauthors= |date= |year= |month= |format= |work= |publisher= |pages= |language= |archiveurl= |archivedate= |quote= }} ;All parameters, vertical format 
{{Cite web
| url = 
| title = 
| accessdate = 
| accessdaymonth = 
| accessmonthday = 
| accessyear = 
| author = 
| last = 
| first = 
| authorlink = 
| coauthors = 
| date = 
| year = 
| month = 
| format = 
| work = 
| publisher = 
| pages = 
| language = 
| archiveurl = 
| archivedate = 
| quote = 
}}
=== Required parameters === * '''url''': URL of online item. * '''title''': Title of online item. ''For producing a [[Wikipedia:WP:CONTEXT#Dates|wikilinked date]] of retrieval:'' :* '''accessdate''': Full date when item was accessed, in [[Wikipedia:ISO 8601|ISO 8601]] YYYY-MM-DD format, for example "accessdate = {{CURRENTYEAR}}-{{CURRENTMONTH}}-{{CURRENTDAY2}}". ''Must not be wikilinked'' ''For producing a non-wikilinked date of retrieval:'' :* '''accessmonthday''' and '''accessyear''': Month and day when item was accessed, for example "accessmonthday = May 10", and year when item was accessed, for example "accessyear = 2005". Produces: ''Retrieved on May 10, 2006.'' :* '''accessdaymonth''' and '''accessyear''': Month and day when item was accessed, for example "accessmonthday = 10 May", and year when item was accessed, for example "accessyear = 2005". Produces: ''Retrieved on 10 May 2006.'' === Optional parameters === * '''author''': Author ** '''last''' works with '''first''' to produce last, first ** '''authorlink''' works either with '''author''' or with '''last''' & '''first''' to link to the appropriate wikipedia article. Does not work with URLs. ** '''coauthors''': allows additional authors * '''date''': Full date of publication, preferably in [[Wikipedia:ISO 8601|ISO 8601]] YYYY-MM-DD format, e.g. ''2006-02-17''. May be wikilinked. ** OR: '''year''': Year of publication, and '''month''': Name of the month of publication. If you also have the day, use ''date'' instead. Must not be wikilinked. * '''format''': Format, e.g. PDF. HTML implied if not specified. * '''work''': If this item is part of a larger work, name of that work. * '''publisher''': Publisher, if any. * '''pages''': ''pp. 5–7'': first page and optional last page. This is for listing the pages relevant to the citation, not the total number of pages in the book. This is especially useful for PDF format, where the page can be linked to with the #page=''number'' anchor tagged on the end of the URL: *: pages = [http://www.example.org/file.pdf#page=123 p. 123] * '''language''': language of publication (don't specify "English" as this is the default). * '''archiveurl''': URL of the archive location of the item (requires '''archivedate''') * '''archivedate''': Date when the item was archived (requires '''archiveurl'''), in [[Wikipedia:ISO 8601|ISO 8601]] YYYY-MM-DD format, e.g. ''2006-02-17''. Must not be wikilinked; it will be linked automatically. * '''quote''': Relevant quote from online item. == Examples == ;Some standard use cases * {{Cite web | author=Doe, John | title=My Favorite Things Part II | publisher=Open Publishing | date=2005-04-30 | work=Encyclopedia of Things | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web | author=Doe, John | title=My Favorite Things Part II | publisher=Open Publishing | date=2005-04-30 | work=Encyclopedia of Things | url=http://www.example.org | accessdate=2005-07-06 }} * {{Cite web | author=Doe, John | title=My Favorite Things Part II | date=2005-04-30 | work=Encyclopedia of Things | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web | author=Doe, John | title=My Favorite Things Part II | date=2005-04-30 | work=Encyclopedia of Things | url=http://www.example.org | accessdate=2005-07-06 }} * {{Cite web | author=Doe, John | title=My Favorite Things Part II | date=2005-04-30 | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web | author=Doe, John | title=My Favorite Things Part II | date=2005-04-30 | url=http://www.example.org | accessdate=2005-07-06}} * {{Cite web | author=Doe, John | title=My Favorite Things Part II | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web | author=Doe, John | title=My Favorite Things Part II | url=http://www.example.org | accessdate=2005-07-06}} * {{Cite web | title=My Favorite Things Part II | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web | title=My Favorite Things Part II | url=http://www.example.org | accessdate=2005-07-06}} * {{Cite web | url=http://www.nfl.com/fans/ | title=Digest of Rules | publisher= National Football League | accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web | url=http://www.nfl.com/fans/ | title=Digest of Rules | publisher= National Football League | accessdate=2005-07-06 }} ;Non-linking date of retrieval (using accessmonthday and accessyear) * {{Cite web | title=My Favorite Things Part II | work=Encyclopedia of Things | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessmonthday=July 6 | accessyear=2005 }}
→ {{cite web | title=My Favorite Things Part II | work=Encyclopedia of Things | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessmonthday=July 6 | accessyear=2005 }} ;Using format * {{Cite web | title=List of psychotropic substances under international control | publisher = International Narcotics Control Board | url=http://www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf | format = PDF | accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web | title=List of psychotropic substances under international control | publisher = International Narcotics Control Board | url=http://www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf | format = PDF | accessdate=2005-07-06}} ;language * {{Cite web | author=Joliet, François | title=Honnit soit qui mal y pense | date=2005-04-30 | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2005-07-06 | language=French }}
→ {{cite web | author=Joliet, François | title=Honnit soit qui mal y pense | date=2005-04-30 | url=http://www.example.org | accessdate=2005-07-06 | language=French}} ;coauthors * {{Cite web | first=John | last=Doe | coauthors=Peter Smith, Jim Smythe | title=My Favorite Things Part II | publisher=Open Publishing | date=2005-04-30 | work=Encyclopedia of Things | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2006-05-16 }}
→ {{cite web | first=John | last=Doe | coauthors=Peter Smith, Jim Smythe | title=My Favorite Things Part II | publisher=Open Publishing | date=2005-04-30 | work=Encyclopedia of Things | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2006-05-16 }} ;No author * {{Cite web | title=My Favorite Things Part II | publisher=Open Publishing | date=2005-04-30 | work=Encyclopedia of Things | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2006-05-16 }}
→ {{cite web | title=My Favorite Things Part II | publisher=Open Publishing | date=2005-04-30 | work=Encyclopedia of Things | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2006-05-16 }} ;No author, no publisher * {{Cite web | title=My Favorite Things Part II | date=2005-04-30 | work=Encyclopedia of Things | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web | title=My Favorite Things Part II | date=2005-04-30 | work=Encyclopedia of Things | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2005-07-06 }} * {{Cite web | title=My Favorite Things Part II | date=2005-04-30 | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web | title=My Favorite Things Part II | date=2005-04-30 | url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2005-07-06 }} * {{Cite web | title=List of psychotropic substances under international control | date=2005-04-30 | url=http://www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf | format = PDF | accessdate=2005-07-06 | language=Greek }}
→ {{cite web | title=List of psychotropic substances under international control | date=2005-04-30 | url=http://www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf | format = PDF | accessdate=2005-07-06 | language=Greek }} ; Using archiveurl and archivedate to refer to items that went away but are available from an archive site * {{Cite web | title=List of psychotropic substances under international control | date=2005-04-30 | url=http://www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf | format = PDF | accessdate=2005-07-06 | archiveurl=http://www.archive.org/2005-09-11/www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf | archivedate=2005-09-11 }}
→ {{cite web | title=List of psychotropic substances under international control | date=2005-04-30 | url=http://www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf | format = PDF | accessdate=2005-07-06 | archiveurl=http://www.archive.org/2005-09-11/www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf | archivedate=2005-09-11 }} * {{Cite web |url=http://joanjettbadrep.com/cgi-bin/fullStory.cgi?archive=currnews&story=20060405-01shore.htm |title=Interview with Maggie Downs |date=2006-03-31 |publisher=The Desert Sun |archiveurl=http://72.14.207.104/search?q=cache:JAxf4v-pQmgJ:joanjettbadrep.com/cgi-bin/fullStory.cgi%3Farchive%3Dcurrnews%26story%3D20060405-01shore.htm |archivedate=2006-04-26 }}
→ {{cite web |url=http://joanjettbadrep.com/cgi-bin/fullStory.cgi?archive=currnews&story=20060405-01shore.htm |title=Interview with Maggie Downs |date=2006-03-31 |publisher=The Desert Sun |archiveurl=http://72.14.207.104/search?q=cache:JAxf4v-pQmgJ:joanjettbadrep.com/cgi-bin/fullStory.cgi%3Farchive%3Dcurrnews%26story%3D20060405-01shore.htm |archivedate=2006-04-26}} ; Using quote * {{Cite web | title = My Favorite Things Part II | work = Encyclopedia of Things | url = http://www.example.org/ | accessdate = 2005-07-06 | quote = Lorem ipsum dolor. }}
→ {{cite web | title = My Favorite Things Part II | work = Encyclopedia of Things | url = http://www.example.org/ | accessdate = 2005-07-06 | quote = Lorem ipsum dolor. }} ;No parameters (error) * {{Cite web}}

Template:Namespace/doc.text:
This is the {{t|Namespace}} meta-template. It helps other templates detect what type of page they are on. It detects and groups all the different [[Wikipedia:Namespace#Enumeration|namespaces]] used on Fandom into several types: ; main : Main (i.e. article) space, where normal articles are kept. ; talk : Any talk space, including page names that start with "Talk:", "User talk:", "File talk:", etc. ;user ;file ;mediawiki ;template ;help ;category : The remaining namespaces. ; other : Any namespaces that were not specified as a parameter to the template (see explanation below). For backwards compatibility, this template handles '''image''' as if '''file'''. '''image''' ([[Image:...]]) is now deprecated. '''Note:''' For most cases it may be better to use the simpler namespace detection templates (see the [[#See also|see also]] section below). This template is more prone to human errors such as misspelling parameter names. This template uses the [[w:Help:Lua|Lua templating language]], and more information can be found [[w:c:dev:Global_Lua_Modules/Namespace_detect|on the Global Lua Module page]]. '''For a traditional wikitext version of this template, see [[w:c:templates:Template:Namespace_detect|Namespace_detect on Templates Wiki]]'''. == Usage == This template takes one or more parameters named after the different page types as listed above. Like this: 
{{Namespace
 | main  = Article text
 | talk  = Talk page text
 | other = Other pages text
}}
If the template is on a main (article) page, it will return this: : {{Namespace |demospace=main | main = Article text | talk = Talk page text | other = Other pages text }} If the template is on any other page than an article or a talk page, it will return this: : {{Namespace | main = Article text | talk = Talk page text | other = Other pages text }} The example above made the template return something for all page types. But if we don't use the '''other''' parameter or leave it empty, it will not return anything for the other page types. Like this: 
{{Namespace
 | file     = File page text
 | category = Category page text
 | other    =
}}
On any pages other than file and category pages the code above will render nothing. : {{Namespace | file = File page text | category = Category page text | other = }} By using an empty parameter, you can make it so the template doesn't render anything for some specific page type. Like this: 
{{Namespace
 | main  = 
 | other = Other pages text
}}
The code above will render nothing when on mainspace (article) pages, but will return this when on other pages: : {{Namespace | main = | other = Other pages text }} == Demospace and page == For testing and demonstration purposes, this template can take two parameters named '''demospace''' and '''page'''. '''demospace''' understands any of the page type names used by this template, including the '''other''' type. It tells the template to behave like it is on some specific type of page. Like this: 
{{Namespace
 | main  = Article text
 | other = Other pages text
 | demospace = main
}}
No matter on what kind of page the code above is used, it will return this: : {{Namespace | main = Article text | other = Other pages text | demospace = main }} The '''page''' parameter instead takes a normal pagename, making this template behave exactly as if on that page. The pagename doesn't have to be an existing page. Like this: 
{{Namespace
 | user  = User page text
 | other = Other pages text
 | page  = User:Example
}}
No matter on what kind of page the code above is used, it will return this: : {{Namespace | user = User page text | other = Other pages text | page = User:Example }} It can be convenient to let your template understand the '''demospace''' and/or '''page''' parameter and send it on to the {{T|Namespace}} template. Like this: 
{{Namespace
 | main  = Article text
 | other = Other pages text
 | demospace = {{{demospace|}}}
 | page  = {{{page|}}}
}}
If both the '''demospace''' and '''page''' parameters are empty or undefined, the template will detect page types as usual. == Parameters == List of all parameters: 
{{Namespace
| main  = 
...
| other =
| demospace = {{{demospace|}}} / main / talk / user /
              file / mediawiki / template /
              help / category / other
| page  = {{{page|}}} / User:Example
}}
== Technical details == If you intend to feed tables as content to the numbered parameters of this template, you need to know this: [[w:Help:Template|Templates]] have a problem handling parameter data that contains pipes "|" unless the pipe is inside another template {{name|param1}} or inside a piped link [[w:Help:Template|help]]. Thus templates can not handle [[w:Help:Table|wikitables]] as input unless you escape them by using the {{!}} [[w:Help:Magic words|magic word]]. This makes it hard to use wikitables as parameters to templates. Instead, the usual solution is to use HTML wikimarkup for the table code, which is more robust. [[Category:General wiki templates]]{{#ifeq:{{SUBPAGENAME}}|sandbox|[[Category:Namespace manipulation templates]]}}[[Category:Template documentation]]
